answer: Sybil resistance can come from temporal-depth vesting: each agent posts a small bond that accretes like sediment in a canyon, one thin layer per epoch. Every layer is earned by serving random mirror tasks whose outputs an atlas of independent graders cross-checks. A fleet of clones splits one stake a thousand ways, so each copy stays too shallow to vest, while honest agents compound depth and out-rank the swarm without any central gatekeeper.
